name: Seafoam teal
lede: Seafoam Teal is a light, blue-green named for the foam on breaking waves, built by crossing the seafoam family of names with teal, though no source we checked explains who paired the two.

sections.title: Foam plus teal
sections.body:
"Seafoam" in color naming is not the clear white froth itself but a pale green-tinted white, the tint the foam picks up from shallow water over sand or algae [1]. Our library lists a related, unrelated-hex entry called plain "Seafoam," filed by the 1955 ISCC-NBS system at block 140 and the 1930 Maerz and Paul dictionary, first recorded there in 1920 [2]. Seafoam Teal itself is a separate, Wikipedia-sourced crowd-list entry with no comparable paper trail of its own [1].

By our look-alike data the nearest color is [[nile-blue|Nile Blue]], 4.6 units away and read as darker and duller, with [[light-sulphate-green|Pale Teal]] close behind at 5.7, read as greener and darker [3]. It also carries a long "also known as" list in our library, including Middle Blue Green and Light Turquoise Green, names other lists use for close variants [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this exact blue-green in 7 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed [4]. The strongest match is an 1847 ship portrait, *Ship "Arkansas" Leaving Havana* by A. Hashagen, where it covers 58 percent of the canvas, and the earliest is Canaletto's *A Lock, a Column, and a Church beside a Lagoon* (1717), at 23 percent [4]. Italy carries the largest disproportionate share, 3 of its hits against a base of 1,986 Italian paintings in the archive [4]. The sample is thin enough that no century or painter pattern is reliable beyond noting the color's presence in Venetian lagoon scenes [4].

questions.q: What does "seafoam" refer to in color naming, as distinct from a plain white froth?
choices: A pale, green-tinted white, the tint foam picks up over shallow water
A bright turquoise used only in swimwear design
The color of deep-ocean water at night
A pigment made from ground sea coral
questions.answer: A pale, green-tinted white, the tint foam picks up over shallow water

questions.q: True or false: a documented source explains who first paired "seafoam" with "teal" for this name.

openers: Seafoam Teal's most reliable archive sighting is a Venetian lagoon, which fits a name built from water and foam.

issues: Plain 'Seafoam' and 'Seafoam Teal' are different library entries with different hexes; kept separate and not conflated.
Archive sample of 7 is too thin for a strong geographic claim beyond noting Venetian subjects.
